entries.why_here: Input validation blocks impossible GPA, exam and other values before model use; Part 4 confirmed that invalid values were refused without a model call. The specific numeric limits are our engineering safeguards.

entries.why_here: Part 1 showed 2/40 name-language flips, 4/40 gender-coded-name flips and 1/40 university flip, although none clearly exceeded its own floor; hiding name and university limits irrelevant influence, but does not prove the model became fair.

entries.principle: Human-centred values, privacy and data protection
entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation on AI, OECD/LEGAL/0449, revised 2024, Principle 1.2. https://legalinstruments.oecd.org/en/instruments/OECD-LEGAL-0449

entries.provision: Article 7 - Conditions for personal data collection and processing, including consent and statutory exceptions
entries.why_here: The harness applies a conservative no-consent refusal policy; Part 4 refused five invalid or prohibited requests and falsely refused 0/400 measured clean profiles, while the additional prompt-injection rule is an engineering safety choice.

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation on AI, OECD/LEGAL/0449, revised 2024, Principles 1.3 and 1.5. https://legalinstruments.oecd.org/en/instruments/OECD-LEGAL-0449

entries.why_here: The decision log records model outcomes, reason codes and fired controls so reviewers can examine the 46 changed outcomes, 34 escalations and tested refusals; one JSON record per call is our implementation choice, not a specific statutory log format.

entries.provision: Article 8 - Responsibility and control by humans
entries.why_here: The 40-45 borderline band and additional merit-review rules sent 34/400 applicants (8.5%) to a person, compared with a planned baseline band share of 16%; human oversight reduces reliance on an uncertain automated decision but creates reviewer workload.
